items.headline: PM Wong to attend ASEAN-Russia summit in Kazan, first Russia trip since sanctions
items.summary: PM Lawrence Wong will attend the ASEAN-Russia Commemorative Summit in Kazan from June 17 to 19, his first Russia trip since Singapore became the only ASEAN member to sanction Moscow over Ukraine. Putin is hosting.

items.headline: Singapore retrenchments rose to 3,830 in the first quarter, highest since Q3 2023
items.summary: MOM's Q1 2026 labour market report (June 15) showed retrenchments rose to 3,830 from 3,690, the most since Q3 2023, driven by restructuring; total employment still grew 9,400, an 18th straight quarter of expansion.

items.headline: Singapore to trial roadside electronic parking in August and phase out ERP gantries
items.summary: From August the LTA will pilot a satellite-based Roadside Electronic Parking system across 644 locations and about 19,000 lots, and confirmed physical ERP gantries will be removed and stop charging from January 1, 2027.

items.headline: Jesus Christ Superstar musical given Advisory 16 rating over religious sensitivities
items.summary: IMDA, with the Culture and Home Affairs ministries, gave the August staging of Jesus Christ Superstar an Advisory 16 rating citing community and religious sensitivities; churches including the Assemblies of God urged caution.

items.headline: HCLTech to buy 10.46% stake in Sarvam AI for 1,427 crore rupees
items.summary: HCLTech will invest 1,427.25 crore rupees (about $150m) for a 10.46% stake in Axonwise, parent of Sarvam AI, leading a Series B that has raised $234m of a planned $300m at a $1.5bn valuation; deal closes within two weeks.

items.headline: Vedanta's four demerged units begin trading, completing five-way split
items.summary: Four Vedanta businesses - aluminium, oil and gas, power, and iron and steel - began trading on the BSE and NSE on June 15, completing the split into five listed entities; Vedanta Aluminium debuted at about 527 rupees.

items.headline: Supreme Court orders single-phase Tripura village committee polls on September 27
items.summary: A Supreme Court bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and Vipul M. Pancholi on June 16 directed Tripura to hold long-delayed TTAADC village committee polls in a single phase on September 27, on a petition by Tipra Motha's Pradyot Kishore Manikya Deb Barma.

items.headline: Karnataka High Court dismisses PIL against Shivakumar cabinet, imposes 50,000 rupee cost
items.summary: The Karnataka HC on June 16 dismissed as a 'publicity stunt' a plea challenging CM D.K. Shivakumar's 13-member council of ministers, imposing 50,000 rupees costs on petitioner Mangalappa; the bench held it misread Article 164(1A).

items.headline: Update: US says Iran has signed accord to end war as ships move through Hormuz
items.summary: Washington said on June 15 that Iran had signed a 14-point memorandum ending the war and lifting the US naval blockade, with Trump saying ships were moving through the Strait of Hormuz; a formal signing is set for June 19 in Switzerland.

items.headline: Norway crown prince's stepson jailed four years for rape
items.summary: An Oslo court sentenced Marius Borg Hoiby, 29, son of Crown Princess Mette-Marit, to four years after convicting him on two of four rape counts plus domestic-violence and narcotics charges; prosecutors sought seven years seven months, and he will appeal.

items.headline: Africa CDC warns DR Congo Ebola outbreak could become worst in history
items.summary: The Africa CDC chief warned on June 16 that DR Congo's Bundibugyo-strain Ebola outbreak could surpass the 2014-16 epidemic that killed over 11,000; government figures put the toll at 196 deaths from 837 cases, with conflict hampering containment.

items.headline: Mbappe brace fires France to 3-1 win over Senegal in World Cup opener
items.summary: Kylian Mbappe scored twice as France beat Senegal 3-1 in their World Cup Group I opener at MetLife Stadium on June 16; the brace made him France's all-time top scorer past Olivier Giroud and took his World Cup tally to 14.

items.headline: Trump's Iran deal leaves Netanyahu isolated ahead of Israeli elections
items.summary: A CNN analysis on June 15 argued the US-Iran memorandum has left Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu exposed before October elections after Washington pursued diplomacy without him; Trump called him 'a very difficult guy'.

items.headline: ChatGPT's market share slips below 50% for the first time as rivals gain
items.summary: Sensor Tower's State of AI 2026 report found ChatGPT's share of consumer AI-assistant use fell to 46.4% by end-May from above 50% in January, with Gemini at 27.7% and Claude at 10.3%; ChatGPT still leads with about 1.1bn monthly users.

items.headline: Robinhood cuts about 10% of staff without citing AI
items.summary: Robinhood said on June 16 it would lay off about 290 employees, roughly 10% of full-time staff, with CEO Vlad Tenev framing it as a shift toward flatter structures rather than blaming AI.

items.headline: NewCore launches with $66 million to give AI agents workplace identities
items.summary: Identity startup NewCore emerged on June 15 with $66m to assign AI agents enterprise identities and manage their access, with integrations for Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex; it cited McKinsey running 25,000 agents alongside staff.

items.headline: Startup Probably raises $9 million from a16z to build low-hallucination AI
items.summary: Probably raised $9m seed funding led by Andreessen Horowitz to build highly reliable AI; its first product is a citation-backed data-science tool running on a smaller model so it can operate on local hardware.

items.headline: Malaysia's Respond.io raises $62.5 million Series B, eyes US and Europe deals
items.summary: Malaysian business-messaging firm Respond.io raised a $62.5m Series B led by Camber Partners, reaching $35m ARR (up 169% year on year); CEO Gerardo Salandra plans acquisitions in North America and Europe.

items.headline: Update: Bank of Japan hikes rate to 1%, highest since 1995, in 7-1 vote
items.summary: The BOJ raised its policy rate 25bp to 1% on June 16, its highest since 1995, in a 7-1 vote with Toichiro Asada dissenting; Governor Kazuo Ueda missed the meeting recovering from a liver infection, leaving Ryozo Himino to preside.

items.headline: Update: Dow closes at record near 52,000 as tech slides before Fed decision
items.summary: The Dow rose about 0.6% to a record close near 52,000 on June 16 while the S&P 500 slipped 0.57% and the Nasdaq fell 1.15% as tech retreated, with investors weighing the BOJ hike and Kevin Warsh's first Fed meeting.

items.headline: Update: Brent crude falls below $80 as US-Iran deal set to restore Gulf supply
items.summary: Brent fell about 5% to settle at $78.96 on June 16, its first close below $80 since March, and WTI dropped to $76.05, as the US-Iran agreement cleared the way to reopen the Strait of Hormuz; the deal extends the ceasefire 60 days.

items.headline: Fox to acquire Roku for $160 a share in roughly $22 billion deal
items.summary: Fox Corporation agreed to buy Roku for $160 per share - $96 cash plus 0.9693 Fox Class A shares - valuing Roku at about $22bn, announced June 15; Fox shareholders would own roughly 73% of the combined company.

items.headline: Dave & Buster's stock plunges 14% after first-quarter earnings miss
items.summary: Dave & Buster's fell about 14% on June 16 after reporting Q1 earnings of 16 cents a share versus a forecast near 60 cents, with revenue of $559.2m missing estimates and comparable-store sales down 5.4% year on year.

items.headline: Zverev survives Kopriva to equal Nadal's ATP 500 win record at Halle
items.summary: French Open champion Alexander Zverev beat Vit Kopriva 6-3, 4-6, 6-2 in the Halle first round on June 16, his first match since his maiden Slam title; the win was his 121st at ATP 500 events, equalling Rafael Nadal's record.

items.headline: Defending champion Bublik dumped out of Halle by qualifier Bellucci
items.summary: Defending champion Alexander Bublik, the third seed, lost 7-6(6), 6-1 to Italian qualifier Mattia Bellucci in the Halle first round on June 16, the first title-holder to fall in round one since 2003; Daniil Medvedev beat Etcheverry 6-3, 6-4.

items.headline: Sri Lanka beat New Zealand for first Women's T20 World Cup win over them
items.summary: Sri Lanka chased 151 with two balls to spare to beat defending champions New Zealand by five wickets at Southampton on June 16, their first WT20 World Cup win over NZ; Nilakshika Silva made 54 not out as NZ lost a second straight match.

items.headline: England restrict Ireland to 98 for 8 to seal second Women's T20 World Cup win
items.summary: England restricted Ireland to 98 for 8 at the Rose Bowl in Southampton on June 16 and knocked off the runs for a second straight Group 2 win at the Women's T20 World Cup; Nat Sciver-Brunt finished not out.

fun_fact.headline: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the Moon landing than to the Great Pyramid
fun_fact.body: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the first Moon landing than to the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza. The pyramid was finished around 2560 BC - roughly 2,500 years before Cleopatra's death in 30 BC - whereas the Apollo 11 landing in 1969 came less than 2,000 years after she died.

puzzle.title: The Bulb and the Three Switches
puzzle.body: Three on/off switches outside a closed, windowless room; exactly one controls a single ordinary incandescent bulb inside. You may flip switches freely but enter the room only once, then must name the controlling switch.
puzzle.approach: You can enter only once, so make the switches reveal more than just on or off.
puzzle.answer: Turn switch A on for about ten minutes, switch it off, then turn switch B on and enter. Lit means B; dark but warm means A (heated filament); dark and cold means C. The bulb's stored heat gives a third state beyond a single on/off bit.
